api/CalculatorLibrary.CalculatorCli.html.summary: Class CalculatorCli Namespace CalculatorLibrary Assembly CalculatorLibrary.dll Parses and runs the calculator's command-line arguments. public static class CalculatorCli Inheritance object CalculatorCli Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The parsing logic lives here, in the library, instead of in CalculatorApp/Program.cs, so it can be unit tested directly (see CalculatorLibrary.Tests/CalculatorCliTests.cs) without spawning the console application as a process. Program.cs only calls Run(string[]) or RunDemo() and prints the result — it never reads from the console, so it never blocks when the app is launched from a script, a build pipeline or CI. When you rename this sample into your own project, replace this class with your own argument-parsing entry point, keeping the same "parsing is a library function, not something the console shell does inline" shape. Fields UsageText The usage line shown when the arguments cannot be parsed. public const string UsageText = "Usage: CalculatorApp <add|subtract|multiply|divide> <a> <b>" Field Value string Methods Run(string[]) Parses args as <operation> <a> <b> and returns a line of text describing the result. public static string Run(string[] args) Parameters args string[] Exactly three arguments: the operation name (add, subtract, multiply or divide, case-insensitive) followed by the two integer operands. Returns string A human-readable line such as "2 add 2 = 4". Exceptions ArgumentException Thrown when the argument count is wrong, an operand is not a valid 32-bit integer, or the operation name is not recognized. The message always ends with UsageText. DivideByZeroException Thrown when dividing by zero. RunDemo() Runs a small built-in demonstration that exercises every operation once, used when the application is started with no arguments at all (so a first run always shows something, without waiting on keyboard input). public static string RunDemo() Returns string The combined demo output, ending with UsageText.
